title: Digital technologies and financial inclusion in Sub-Saharan Africa
decision_rationale: Quantitative panel study (system GMM and IV-Tobit) of ICT indicators (internet, mobile, fixed broadband, fixed telephone, composite) in 43 economies; outcome is financial inclusion (family 5).
exposure_measure: Internet users, fixed broadband, fixed telephone and mobile cellular subscriptions (per 100 people, WDI) and a composite digitalization indicator; each entered separately

sample.income_groups_covered: not reported (region-only sample; no income-group split)

design.estimator: System GMM (forward orthogonal deviations, time dummies) as main; IV-Tobit as baseline
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: FDI, GDP per capita, consumption, savings, inflation, trade; time effects; lagged dependent variable; explanatory variables treated as exogenous; internal (lag-residual) instruments in IV-Tobit

results.indicator: Bank accounts per 100,000 adults (system GMM, internet users)
ATMs per 100,000 adults (system GMM, internet users)
Financial inclusion index, PCA composite (system GMM, digitalization)

n_specifications_reported: about 35 (5 technology measures x 4 outcomes in GMM, 3 outcomes in IV-Tobit)

confounding_reverse_causation.why: Causal language ('digital technology increases financial inclusion'); GMM with all regressors declared exogenous and only time dummies as instruments; internal IV-Tobit instruments are lags. Reverse causality not credibly handled.
confounding_reverse_causation.evidence: Section 4.2, p.7: 'all our explanatory are treated as exogenous'

exposure_measurement.why: Standard WDI subscription counts, adequate for ICT diffusion; composite indicator construction not detailed.

selection_of_countries_years.why: 43 SSA countries chosen by data availability; effective sample falls to 29-37 countries; some countries dropped.

outcome_measurement.why: Financial inclusion proxied by supply-side bank accounts, branches and ATMs; mixed units (per 100,000 adults) and min-max normalisation; variables such as deposits and credit are financial depth, not inclusion. Text also states bank-account figures 'per 100,000 people' and 'mobile money subscribers' inconsistently.

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: Lagged dependent variable coefficients near or above 1 (1.003, 1.031, 1.050), indicating unit root/non-stationarity; AR(2) and Hansen p-values marginal in places (Table 7); instrument count 24-25; many specifications.

selective_reporting.why: All reported technology coefficients positive and significant; robustness composite index results reported only partly; credit, deposits and loans outcomes mentioned in text but not tabulated.

notes: Telecommunications Policy 2022. Digital technology effect is on financial inclusion only; GDP per capita is a control, not an outcome. Dependent variables min-max normalised to 0-1 while coefficients are on different scales across tables. The text states country-count discrepancies (43 countries; 'individuals greater than time series'). No text aimed at the extractor found.
